title: Product projections and clopen graph images commute with base change
statement: Let $p:U\to Y$, $q:V\to Y$, and $i:Y_0\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $q$ finite etale [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Form $U_0=U\times_Y Y_0$, $V_0=V\times_Y Y_0$, $P=V\times_Y U$, and $P_0=V_0\times_{Y_0}U_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $t:U_0\to U$, $j:P_0\to P$ for the canonical maps and $r:P\to U$, $r_0:P_0\to U_0$ for the projections. Then the square with maps $(j,r_0,r,t)$ is cartesian. For every $a:U\to V$ over $Y$, let $a_0:U_0\to V_0$ be its base change. The image of the graph of $a_0$ is exactly $j^{-1}$ of the image of the graph of $a$.

source.place: mk' (364–381), of_right (231–235); Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/OpenImmersion.lean, range_pullbackSnd (636); corrected blueprint steps 1–3

proof.text: Prove the product square cartesian directly by its universal property: given a:T→P and b:T→U0 with matching U projections, lift the V projection of a and Y0 projection of b to V0, then lift that map and b to P0. Projection identities verify the two required equations. Uniqueness is checked by successive pullback.hom_ext on P0 and V0. This is IsPullback.mk' in the delivered proof.

The graph sections s and s0 obey s0≫j=t≫s by their two product projections. Compose this square on the right with the cartesian product square. Its outer square has both horizontal maps identity, hence is cartesian; cancellation of the right square (IsPullback.of_right) proves the graph square cartesian.

The graph s is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Its cartesian base change is the open subscheme given by the inverse image of its image [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. Transport the second projection across the canonical pullback isomorphism. Its range is unchanged by that isomorphism, and IsOpenImmersion.range_pullbackSnd (OpenImmersion.lean:636) gives exactly the desired equality.

blueprint_update.statement: Let $p:U\to Y$, $q:V\to Y$, and $i:Y_0\to Y$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $q$ finite etale. Form $U_0=U\times_Y Y_0$, $V_0=V\times_Y Y_0$, $P=V\times_Y U$, and $P_0=V_0\times_{Y_0}U_0$. Write $t:U_0\to U$, $j:P_0\to P$ for the canonical maps and $r:P\to U$, $r_0:P_0\to U_0$ for the projections. Then the square with maps $(j,r_0,r,t)$ is cartesian. For every $a:U\to V$ over $Y$, let $a_0:U_0\to V_0$ be its base change. The image of the graph of $a_0$ is exactly $j^{-1}$ of the image of the graph of $a$.

proof.text: *The product square.* Given $a:T\to P$ and $b:T\to U_0$ with $r\circ a=t\circ b$, the $V$-component of $a$ and the $Y_0$-component of $b$ define a morphism $T\to V_0$, and together with $b$ a morphism $T\to P_0$; the projection identities show that it is compatible with $a$ and $b$. Uniqueness follows by checking components on the fibre products $P_0$ and $V_0$. Hence $(j,r_0,r,t)$ is cartesian.

*The graph square.* Let $s=(a,\mathrm{id}_U):U\to P$ and $s_0=(a_0,\mathrm{id}_{U_0}):U_0\to P_0$ be the graph sections. Comparing the two product projections gives $j\circ s_0=s\circ t$. Pasting this square with the cartesian product square gives the outer square with identities as horizontal maps, which is cartesian; by cancellation the graph square is cartesian.

*Images.* Since $q$ is etale and separated, the section $s$ of the etale projection $r$ is an open immersion. The base change of an open immersion along $j$ is the open subscheme $j^{-1}(s(U))$ of $P_0$, and by the graph square this base change is $s_0$ up to isomorphism. Hence the image of $s_0$ equals $j^{-1}$ of the image of $s$.
